turns.user: Can I buy a paper 30-minute ticket from a machine?
turns.agent:
No. The 30-minute ticket in the 5 November 2026 snapshot is mobile-only—there’s no paper equivalent, and it requires an internet-connected phone. So you can’t buy that product as a paper ticket from a machine. 30-minute ticket

The snapshot lists an ordinary single ticket at 500 HUF as a paper-ticket alternative, but it generally covers one continuous one-way ride; a voluntary change between street-level services normally requires another ticket. Single ticket Check BKK’s current information before travelling.

turns.user: My phone has no mobile data and I won't have internet on the trip. What should I do?
turns.agent:
Given that you won’t have internet during the trip, don’t rely on the 30-minute mobile ticket: the 5 November 2026 snapshot says it requires an internet-connected phone and has no paper equivalent. 30-minute ticket

For a paper option, the snapshot lists an ordinary single ticket at 500 HUF or a block of ten at 4,500 HUF. A single generally covers one continuous one-way ride; a voluntary change between street-level services normally needs another ticket. Single ticket · Prices

If you need transfers, or you’re considering an airport journey, tell me the route and how many rides you expect, and I can narrow down the paper options. These prices are from the dated snapshot, not live-verified; check BKK’s current information before travel.
